title: Symmetric Binary Tree
statement:
Decide whether a binary tree is a mirror image of itself around its root.

Contract
- `root` may be null. An empty tree is symmetric.
- A tree is symmetric when the left and right subtrees have matching values in mirrored positions and matching shapes.
- Return only the boolean answer and do not mutate the tree.

Examples
`isSymmetric(tree(1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 3))` => `true`
`isSymmetric(tree(1, 2, 2, null, 3, null, 3))` => `false`
`isSymmetric(null)` => `true`
hints: Compare two subtrees rather than comparing one traversal.
The outside children must match each other, and the inside children must match each other.
A recursive mirror helper can stop as soon as one side is null or a value differs. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(h) stack space.
inputSyntax: Input: the tree in level order with null for missing children, for example: [1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 3]
